title: Joining Speed Webb's band in Muncie
summary: Speed Webb, riding on a movie appearance, takes Wilson, Gus and Roy Eldridge to Muncie and assembles a band including Vic Dickenson and Reunald Jones.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: So a guy named Speed Webb came to town, to Detroit, and I guess this was still in 1929, late in the year, and he had just made a movie called On With the Show, where he was a bandleader in that, and the star of that was Ethel Waters.

And the hit song from On With the Show, was the song, 'Am I Blue,' and so Speed Webb, since he had prominent spot as a bandleader in the movie, he wanted to tour and do personal appearances, so he picked up me and my brother, Gus, and Roy Eldridge from Detroit and took us down to his home town in Muncie, Indiana, and he got Vic Zach Dickenson away from the White band, or the West Helmet band, another road band; and we spent oh, a couple of weeks down there in Muncie rehearsing, and he got some other musicians
from Indiana, Reunald Jones from the Atlanta band; Reunald Jones finally wound up, some years ago, he was lead trumpet fo Basie, back about 20 years ago.
Yeah, but that was senior, now.
Oh yeah, I'm talking about senior. Jonesey we called him.

So the Speed Webb band had Jonesey on one trumpet, Roy Eldridge on the other, Vic Dickenson on one trombone and my brother on the other trombone -- and that was the brass section, two trumpets and two trombones, until later on, we finally found an excellent trumpet player from Louisville who had modeled his mute playing after the great Joe Smith of those days, and played sweet solos in the mute --a guy named Steve Dunn. And that made the brass section.
By the way, do you remember who the drummer was?
Yeah, Scottie his name was, from Pennsylvania. I think Scottie was from Pittsburgh, but I can't think of his whole name, it was just Scottie.
Well, there's a guy, there's a star in California now that used to play with one of those bands. He's the star of one of the television shows, they played out of Cincinat with one of those bands.
Yes. He plays the guitar and the ukelele now on TV. Well, we'll get back to it.
Really? Well, I may think of it, yet, because there are so many of those bands that come to mind -- Wes Helms, as I already mentioned, Zach Whyte --
Zach Whyte's band -- that's it. same

Zach Whyte's band at that time. It was and my brother with Speed, Sy Oliver was with Zach Whyte, and Roy and Vic and I -- Zach had a great pianist, Herman Chittison -- and Quentin Jackson, everyone knows as 'Butter', was a trombone player with Zach. (End of side 1)
